H6KY01110.name: James R. Comer
H6KY01110.bio: U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 1st District and Chairman of the House Oversight Committee; former Kentucky Commissioner of Agriculture and state representative.

H6KY01169.name: John "Drew" Williams
H6KY01169.bio: Murray State University history graduate who has worked in his family's boat dock building business since age 14.

positions.stance: Proposes extending Medicaid eligibility to full-time farmers and farmhands earning under $50,000 and helping family farms withstand disasters and trade disruptions.
Proposes four-term limits for House and Senate members, a lifetime ban on paid lobbying after leaving office, and a congressional stock trading ban.
Proposes a cost-of-living-based regional wage system, stronger wage theft enforcement, and a guarantee of five paid sick days for every worker.
Proposes a 15% per-dose profit margin cap on essential medications and capping brand-name drug prices at 1.5 to 2 times other OECD countries.
Proposes modernizing business size classifications and raising federal small-business contracting goals from 23% to 25%.

H8KY02031.name: S. Brett Guthrie
H8KY02031.bio: U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 2nd District and chairman of the House Energy and Commerce Committee; Army veteran, former manufacturing executive and Kentucky state senator.

H6KY02068.name: Megan Wingfield
H6KY02068.bio: Bowling Green mechanic trained in automotive technology at SKYCTC, caregiver and community activist.

positions.stance: Has signed the U.S. Term Limits pledge and says she will "fight for term limits in Congress."
Wants an economy where one job is enough to support a family, workers are paid a living wage, and small towns thrive.
"Healthcare is a human right"; supports universal, affordable, accessible healthcare, an end to medical debt, and investment in rural communities.
Supports protecting "reproductive freedom and the right to choose" and expanding access to contraception, maternal care, and cancer screenings.
Supports universal Pre-K, affordable childcare, and increased funding for early childhood programs.

H2KY03206.name: Morgan McGarvey
H2KY03206.bio: U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 3rd District; former Kentucky state senator and Senate Minority Leader.

positions.stance: "I believe health care is a basic human right"; supports Medicare for All and allowing Medicare to negotiate drug prices.
Supports expanding public education to include universal pre-Kindergarten and free community college, and funding public universities to make them affordable.
Supports federal spending and tax incentives to dramatically expand renewable energy and a federal clean energy standard for utilities.

H6KY03223.name: Maria Teresa Rodriguez
H6KY03223.bio: Trauma nurse in Louisville and former small business owner who immigrated from Cuba.

positions.stance: "Free markets, not government control"; says she will always fight socialism and protect small businesses.
"Law and order matters"; supports police and cracking down on violent crime to keep neighborhoods safe.
"Less regulation. More growth. Better jobs." Says Washington should help workers succeed, not get in their way.
"Kentucky families deserve to keep more of what they earn"; will fight wasteful spending and tax hikes.
"America is a nation of laws"; supports legal immigration and keeping the borders secure.

H6KY04171.name: Ed Gallrein
H6KY04171.bio: Fifth-generation Kentucky farmer and retired Navy SEAL officer who served three decades and rose to the rank of Captain.

positions.stance: Will work to cut taxes, reduce regulations, stop reckless spending that drove up inflation, and bring good-paying jobs back to Kentucky.
Will work to finish the wall, fully fund Border Patrol and ICE, secure the border, and rebuild the military.
Will protect the right to keep and bear arms "without compromise" and "back the blue."
Describes himself as pro-life: "Gallrein is Pro-Life!"
Will work to eliminate DEI programs, restore merit, and promote patriotism in schools, the military, and government.

H6KY04189.name: Melissa Claire Strange
H6KY04189.bio: Supply chain director for a global nutrition and agribusiness company, where she has worked for almost 27 years.

positions.stance: Wants to protect and expand Medicare, Medicaid, and Social Security and lower prescription drug costs.
Supports small businesses, American manufacturing, career and technical education, Kentucky workers and unions, and protecting pensions.
Supports re-introducing and expanding the Child Tax Credit, paid family leave, universal Pre-K, and a caregivers tax credit.
Supports designating the Red River Gorge National Geologic Area as the Red River Gorge National Park.
Supports term limits, banning congressional stock trading, banning members from becoming lobbyists, and ending Citizens United.

H0KY05015.name: Hal Rogers
H0KY05015.bio: U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 5th District since 1981 and Dean of the U.S. House of Representatives.

H6KY05152.name: Ned Pillersdorf
H6KY05152.bio: Attorney who has run an "underdog/poverty volume law practice" for 44 years and been involved with several nonprofits.

positions.stance: Opposes proposed cuts to Medicaid, Medicare, food stamps, utility assistance, public broadcasting, Job Corps and cancer research to fund a "deficit busting tax break."
"I support Uncapping the House."

H6KY06192.name: Ralph Alvarado
H6KY06192.bio: Physician who has cared for patients in Central Kentucky for nearly three decades; elected to the Kentucky General Assembly in 2014.

positions.stance: Will work with Republicans and Democrats to fix healthcare, lower costs, increase transparency, and give patients more control over their care.
Plans to bring down the cost of groceries, gas, and healthcare, grow good-paying Kentucky jobs, and eliminate wasteful government spending that drives up inflation.

H6KY06184.name: Zach Dembo
H6KY06184.bio: Veteran, former teacher, and former federal prosecutor.

positions.stance: Will "fight to end this senseless trade war" and support free and open trade that helps farmers and distillers compete globally.
Supports Ukraine, protecting Taiwan's sovereignty, and de-escalating the war in Iran; says "I oppose illegal and unnecessary wars."
Supports banning congressional stock trading, a lifetime lobbying ban for former members, ending dark money, and making the Justice Department independent.
Says everyone should make a living wage of at least $15 an hour; will "fully support the PRO Act" and defend the right to unionize.
Will fight to fully fund public schools and job training programs, fairly pay teachers, and maintain university research funding.

H2OR01133.name: Suzanne Bonamici
H2OR01133.bio: Member of Congress and former Oregon state representative and state senator who began her career at Legal Aid and as a consumer rights attorney.

positions.stance: Supports raising the federal minimum wage, enforcing antitrust laws, and repealing Trump's tax cuts so "those at the very top pay their fair share."
Working to pass legislation providing 12 weeks of paid family leave and at least seven job-protected paid sick or safe days.
Says Congress must immediately increase affordable housing supply, including more funding for the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit.
"Health care is a human right"; says all proposals for universal coverage, including Medicare for All, must be on the table.
Describes herself as "a strong proponent of public education" and is committed to public schools where educators have the resources they need.

H6OR01308.name: Barbara Kahl
H6OR01308.bio: Veterinarian (DVM) who has served Oregon communities for over 30 years.

positions.stance: Lists economic growth as her first priority: small business support, infrastructure investment, and jobs that keep families in Oregon.
Supports "Stronger Public Schools, School Choice, Teacher Freedom, Vocational Pathways, and funding that follows the student."
Supports lowering health care costs, strengthening care for veterans, and ensuring quality healthcare reaches every corner of the district.
Supports "responsible stewardship that sustains both the environment and timber-dependent communities."
Supports expanding housing supply at every price point, streamlining permitting, and federal incentives to reduce financing barriers for first-time buyers.

H0OR02127.name: Cliff Bentz
H0OR02127.bio: Rancher, farmer, attorney and former Oregon state legislator who served eight years on the Oregon Water Resources Commission.

positions.stance: Will "protect and defend Farmers' and Ranchers' use of water and the ownership and priority of water rights."
Says the USMCA and the China trade agreement benefit Oregon farmers and ranchers and help ensure "fairness and more free trade."
Will join President Trump in stopping illegal immigration by improving border security and "building/completing the wall."
Will work to strengthen the economy by directing investments toward rural Oregon, reducing regulations, and lowering taxes.
"I am a right to life candidate"; supports an exception to the prohibition on abortion only when the mother's life is at risk.

H6OR02322.name: Chris Beck
H6OR02322.bio: Former Oregon state representative, land conservation nonprofit worker, and USDA policy advisor on rural economic development.

positions.stance: Says Congress must repeal HR 1 "as soon as possible" and restore the funding it cut from Medicaid and SNAP benefits.
Says "we can start by ending the war and canceling tariffs" to address high fuel, housing, and food costs.
Proposes adjusting tax breaks on vacation and luxury homes to fund low-interest financing for first-time rural home buyers.
Supports phasing in "an affordable public care option for all Americans" and incentivizing doctors and nurses to practice in rural areas.
Supports repealing the tariffs, expanding working-lands conservation programs, and establishing a rural service corps to restore forests and watersheds.

H4OR03192.name: Maxine Dexter
H4OR03192.bio: Pulmonary and critical care physician serving in her first term in Congress; former Oregon state legislator.

positions.stance: Wants substance use disorder treatment made accessible and affordable, more detox beds, and criminal justice reform "prioritizing effective treatment over punishment."
Supports increasing the federal minimum wage to $15/hour, tying it to inflation, and eliminating the lower minimum wage for tipped workers.
Will "champion a swift transition to 100% renewable energy sources to eliminate our reliance on fossil fuels."
Supports ensuring every American has affordable health care "with the ultimate goal of a single-payer model."
Makes restoring trust in the federal government a top priority, including holding the Trump administration accountable; has pushed for Trump's impeachment.

H2OR04095.name: Val Hoyle
H2OR04095.bio: Member of Congress; former Oregon Labor Commissioner, state representative, and Oregon House Democratic Majority Leader.

positions.stance: Supports universal preschool, capping childcare costs, comprehensive paid family and medical leave, and passing the PRO Act.
Supports restoring the ACA's enhanced premium tax credits, lowering drug costs, and going after grocery conglomerates that unfairly raise prices.
Will fight to protect vote-by-mail, overturn Citizens United, and pass federal reforms ending partisan gerrymandering nationwide.
Supports passing universal health care legislation and requiring drug companies to offer prescription drugs at a fair price.
Supports major investments in affordable housing, a new renter tax credit, and expanded down-payment assistance for first-time homebuyers.

H6OR04260.name: Monique DeSpain
H6OR04260.bio: Retired Air Force Colonel with 30 years of service in the U.S. Air Force and Oregon National Guard, and a lawyer.

positions.stance: "I will oppose a national abortion ban in Congress"; says women's healthcare decisions "belong between women and their doctors, not the government."
Supports border barriers, sensors and a staffed Border Patrol, closing asylum loopholes, and a one-time path to lawful status for long-settled, non-criminal residents.
Will fight to remove VA bureaucratic obstacles and ensure veteran benefits are protected.
"I support the rule of law and the men and women of law enforcement and other emergency responders."
Says homelessness "cannot have a single solution"; supports expanded help for veterans experiencing homelessness.

H4OR05304.name: Janelle Bynum
H4OR05304.bio: U.S. Congresswoman, former Oregon state legislator, businesswoman, and engineer.

positions.stance: Has introduced legislation to tackle housing shortages and affordability barriers and expand pathways to homeownership; will keep "fighting to make homeownership a reality."
Focused on creating good jobs close to home, supporting small businesses and rural economies, and bringing down the cost of living.
Believes every child deserves a high-quality education; introduced legislation to equip schools, support educators, and expand mental health and special education services.
Has been outspoken against the Trump administration's "attempted takeover of Oregon" and economic policies she says sent costs skyrocketing.
Supports generating more clean energy, transitioning away from fossil fuels, and protecting communities and land from wildfires.

H6OR05242.name: Patti Adair
H6OR05242.bio: Deschutes County Commissioner since 2018 and a CPA.

positions.stance: "Make everyday life more affordable for working-class Oregonians."
"Fully support law enforcement to keep our communities safe."
"Ensure sustainable management of our natural resources."
"Unleash economic growth and support small businesses."
"Ban insider trading by Members of Congress."

H2OR06066.name: Andrea Salinas
H2OR06066.bio: U.S. Congresswoman and former Oregon state legislator who chaired the House Health Care Committee.

positions.stance: Committed to lowering costs for families and bringing more living-wage jobs to Oregon; says she will fight for working Oregonians, "not big corporations."
Will continue to push for prescription drug price caps and allowing Medicare to negotiate drug prices.
Co-chairs the Mental Health Caucus and is committed to improving access to mental health care across America.
Describes herself as an "unwavering champion of abortion access" and says reproductive health care, including abortion, is "essential health care."
Says it is time to invest in affordable housing, expand mental health services, fund addiction treatment, and get unhoused people into housing.

H2OR01240.name: David Russ
H2OR01240.bio: Businessman and former Mayor of Dundee, Oregon.

positions.stance: Lists returning manufacturing to America, ending "onerous Regulations," and stopping subsidies "that only benefit large Corps" under affordability for working families.
Wants to protect small businesses and family farms and "End the IRS manhunt of 1099 employers and employees."
Supports returning federal public lands to state and local control and ending federal control of local schools, utilities, businesses and infrastructure.
Calls for ending "Congressional 10th Amendment Violations" under defending constitutional rights.
Wants to "Make it a federal felony to aide and/or abet illegal border crossers."

H6OK01201.name: John Croisant
H6OK01201.bio: Former teacher and coach, local businessman, and community volunteer.

positions.stance: Supports investment in special education and a federal program helping people graduate debt-free if they teach in public schools for five years.
Supports expanding access through Medicaid expansion, ACA subsidies, or broader universal coverage; will fight to repeal recent federal Medicaid cuts.
Says HUD should focus on supporting local communities and building affordable housing, including more affordable rentals and homes to purchase.
Supports overturning Citizens United, ending stock trading for all branches of government, a five-year lobbying ban, and Supreme Court ethics reform.
Says America should focus on its own internal affairs, "not starting nor continuing forever wars around the world."

H6OK01235.name: Mark Tedford
H6OK01235.bio: Tulsa-area businessman in insurance and construction for more than 30 years and former Oklahoma state legislator.

positions.stance: Will fight for lower costs by reducing inflationary spending, cutting red tape for small businesses, and lowering energy and regulatory costs.
Supports strict enforcement of immigration laws, ending all benefits for illegal immigrants, and deporting criminal aliens; "Citizens must come first."
Wants to eliminate waste, fraud, and abuse, increase transparency in federal spending, and protect Social Security for Americans.
Supports unleashing American energy production, cutting taxes, and growing manufacturing and skilled trades.
Will defend constitutional rights, parental rights, religious liberty, and the Second Amendment.

H2OK02315.name: Josh Brecheen
H2OK02315.bio: Fourth-generation rancher and small heavy equipment and trucking business operator; former Oklahoma state senator.

positions.stance: Says the most effective way to reduce Washington's influence in daily life is "to pass term limits on Members of Congress."
Says term limits are the most effective solution to eliminate corruption in Washington and pledges to honor his term limits pledge again.
"We must close the border except to those who come here through the legal process."
"The education of children in America is a parental responsibility"; says "There should be no federal role in education."
Blames inflation on government interference in the economy; says "The remedy for inflation is to stop government's runaway spending."

H4OK02196.name: Brandon Wade
H4OK02196.bio: Third-generation union worker in Bartlesville who has spent 26 years as a leader with IUOE Local 351.

positions.stance: Supports more trained border agents, surveillance technology "rather than physical barriers," more immigration judges, and ending masked enforcement raids.
Believes "Roe v. Wade should be codified into federal law to guarantee the right to privacy in healthcare decisions."
Wants public funds directed to public schools, not private institutions, and opposes efforts to dismantle the U.S. Department of Education.
Supports eliminating the Social Security payroll tax cap and opposes any effort to cut Medicare benefits.
"Healthcare should not be tied to employment"; supports a nationwide system guaranteeing affordable coverage, exploring Medicare for All or regulated insurance models.

H4OK06056.name: Frank Lucas
H4OK06056.bio: U.S. Representative from Oklahoma and a wheat farmer and cattle rancher.

positions.stance: Believes protecting law-abiding citizens' ability to bear arms is a fundamental right and that "every life is worth protecting- including the life of an unborn child."
Supports Oklahoma's farmers, increased rural broadband, saving rural hospitals, and more "fair and free trade" with trading partners.
Says America must keep its promise to veterans, who "deserve easy access to the benefits they earned."
Supports doing more to secure the Southern border, more resources for border patrol, prioritizing high-skilled entrepreneurs, and streamlining agricultural worker programs.
Supports lowering taxes, reducing burdensome regulations, and increasing free and fair trade.
